catalog_quote: 2.1.4. Stress. Any account of Coeur d'Alene stress will require reference to the stress weight or accent of individual morphemes to account for pairs such as the following, where two roots are subject to the same derivation but result in different stress assignments: x̣esísgʷel //√x̣es=isgʷel// 'edible fish' péqsgʷel //√peq=isgʷel// 'halibut (white fish)' ... There are several categories of Coeur d'Alene morphemes that are never assigned stress: prefixes; pronominal suffixes; vowelless morphemes; most transitivizing suffixes ... Also, the following vowels are never stressed: /e/ of a (lexical) suffix or of the very common morpheme-final element -eʔ ... schwa (/ə/), no matter the source; /u/ and /i/ that result from glide vocalization. The tendency in Coeur d'Alene is to penultimate or final stress or, more accurately, to stress on the penultimate or final stressable vowel ... In sequenc…

sources.quote: sec. 68: 'Since it is one of the chief grammatical devices, stress accent is of the greatest importance in Coeur d'Alene. Every word of more than one syllable has a definite stress which remains stable, or changes for cause. tone.quote: In both cases the word-fmal stressed vowel is subject to an optional rule of stressed vowel lengthening, where the duration of the vowel is extended beyond that of other, phonologically predictable long (unstressed) vowels, and its pitch is raised, giving the vowel a song-like quality. … Stressed vowel lengthening is a discourse device used to indicate some unusual augmentation, either of amount, effort, or duration of the item or action indicated. … (37) ExmNSION: increase stressed vowel duration and raise pitch.

sources.note: A transformational-generative phonology of Coeur d'Alene reanalysing Reichard's 1939 stem list (per Bischoff et al. 2014 commentary); expected to treat stress as morphologically/lexically conditioned and to have no tone section, Coeur d'Alene being a stress language without lexical tone; would be the earliest full phonology and predates Johnson 1975.
